abstract_sentences.text: Learning stationary policies in infinite-horizon general-sum Markov games (MGs) remains a fundamental open problem in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL).

evidence.anchor: Learning stationary policies in infinite-horizon general-sum Markov games (MGs) remains a fundamental open problem in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL).

abstract_sentences.text: While stationary strategies are preferred for their practicality, computing stationary forms of classic game-theoretic equilibria is computationally intractable—a stark contrast to the comparative ease of solving single-agent RL or zero-sum games.

evidence.anchor: While stationary strategies are preferred for their practicality, computing stationary forms of classic game-theoretic equilibria is computationally intractable—a stark contrast to

abstract_sentences.connection: contrasts against single-agent RL and zero-sum games

abstract_sentences.text: To bridge this gap, we study Risk-averse Quantal response Equilibria (RQE), a solution concept rooted in behavioral game theory that incorporates risk aversion and bounded rationality.

evidence.anchor: To bridge this gap, we study Risk-averse Quantal response Equilibria (RQE), a solution concept rooted in behavioral game theory that incorporates risk aversion and bounded rational

abstract_sentences.text: We demonstrate that RQE possesses strong regularity conditions that make it uniquely amenable to learning in MGs.

evidence.anchor: We demonstrate that RQE possesses strong regularity conditions that make it uniquely amenable to learning in MGs.

abstract_sentences.text: We propose a novel single-timescale Actor-Critic algorithm characterized by a faster actor and a slower critic.

evidence.anchor: We propose a novel single-timescale Actor-Critic algorithm characterized by a faster actor and a slower critic.

abstract_sentences.text: Leveraging the regularity of RQE, we prove that this approach achieves global convergence with finite-sample guarantees.

evidence.anchor: Leveraging the regularity of RQE, we prove that this approach achieves global convergence with finite-sample guarantees.

abstract_sentences.text: We empirically validate our algorithm in several environments to demonstrate superior convergence properties compared to risk-neutral baselines.

evidence.anchor: We empirically validate our algorithm in several environments to demonstrate superior convergence properties compared to risk-neutral baselines.

method_summary.formal_input: Finite two-player discounted Markov game plus D_i, nu_i, tau_i, epsilon_i and lambda.

method_summary.objective: Risk-adjusted player objective against a constrained imaginary adversary.
method_summary.algorithm_invariants: Projection keeps policies in simplexes; Algorithm 1 initializes policies uniformly and Q at zero.
method_summary.complexity_statement: No asymptotic runtime/memory complexity. Remark C.1 says extra adversary actors retain same statistical complexity.

final_judgment.single_storyline: Risk aversion and bounded rationality alter the agent objective; the four-player game can be lambda-monotone, which yields regular RQE, Bellman contraction and faster-actor/slower-critic coupled analysis.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: Definitions, theorem statements, coupled update, Figures 1–7 and Table 1 retain decision-facing content.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Proofs, network/replay implementation, environment details, hyperparameters and per-run curves move to pp. 14–63.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 1 → Figure 2 → Figure 3 → Figures 4–7 follows mechanism, condition, behavior and training evidence.
final_judgment.largest_gap: The theorem closes for assumption-heavy tabular Algorithm 1; deep Algorithm 2 lacks matched component ablation, inferential statistics and operational-scale evidence.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: Connect a behavior-side regularizer from objective meaning through structural property and update rule to a compatible observation.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: Do not generalize when preference changes lack task meaning, assumptions cannot be checked, or controls change several mechanisms.
final_judgment.evidence_note: Core evidence: pp. 2–9; detailed proofs/reproduction material: pp. 14–63.
